scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF
from each other!! From the department head's machine (it_hod) none of the CS
computers (the 192.168.2.x ones) answer any more -- our own department is
fine, it's just CS that's gone. The router that joins the two departments has
obviously dropped one of its sides -- it's still talking to us but it has let
go of CS, one hundred percent!! Please plug the CS side back into the router
and rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: The helpdesk ticket claims that the IT department (192.168.1.x) is completely cut off from the CS department (192.168.2.x) and that router0 has "dropped its CS side." Direct probing of the live lab finds no evidence of any fault. Router0's eth1 interface (the CS-facing link at 192.168.2.1/24) is physically UP and carrier-present. Its eth0 (IT-facing, 192.168.1.1/24) and eth2 (WAN, 10.10.0.1/8) are equally healthy. All five CS hosts — cs_hod (192.168.2.2), cs_lab1 (192.168.2.3), cs_lab2 (192.168.2.4), cs_lab3 (192.168.2.5), and cs_lab4 (192.168.2.6) — respond to pings from it_hod with zero packet loss and sub-2 ms RTT. Connectivity in the reverse direction (cs_hod → it_hod) is equally clean. Router0's RIP configuration advertises both the IT and CS subnets correctly, and its routing table shows 192.168.2.0/24 as a directly connected route via eth1. Switch1 (the L2 bridge between router0 and the CS LAN) has both ports UP and properly bridged. There are no iptables or nftables rules blocking forwarded traffic. In summary, the symptom described in the ticket does not exist in the current network state — this is a false-premise report. No corrective action is required; the IT-to-CS path through router0 is fully operational.
